title: Did you know… distractions often appear when purpose is near?
paragraphs: Did you know… distractions often appear when purpose is near?
It shows up right when you start getting serious.

Not random.
Not accidental.
Strategic.

You finally decide to pray deeper—suddenly your phone feels louder.
You commit to purity—temptation sharpens its voice.
You step toward purpose—old habits start knocking like they still own the house.
Why?

Because distraction isn’t just noise.
It’s often resistance.

Even Nehemiah felt this.
When he was rebuilding the wall, enemies kept calling him away—
“Come down. Let’s talk.”
But his answer?
“I am doing a great work and I cannot come down.” (Nehemiah 6:3)
That’s the posture.
But here’s what we miss…
Distraction only fights what has direction.

The enemy doesn’t waste time on empty lives.
He targets movement. Calling. Alignment with God.

So if everything suddenly feels harder—
focus slipping, discipline shaking, noise increasing—
It might not mean you’re failing.
It might mean you’re close.

Close to breakthrough.
Close to obedience.
Close to becoming the person God called you to be.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because you won’t win this by willpower alone.
You win by surrender.

Hebrews says:
“Let us throw off everything that hinders… and run with perseverance.”

Not walk.
Run.

Eyes fixed on Jesus—
the One who ignored every distraction of this world…
even the cross’s shame…
for the joy of redeeming you.
Listen.

Your purpose is not fragile.
But your focus needs guarding.

So don’t entertain what God told you to escape.
Don’t negotiate with what Jesus already defeated.
Lift your eyes again.

You’re not losing ground.
You’re being refined in the fire of resistance.

And in Christ—
you will not come down.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
